text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — streaming-prod-us-east-1: sustained GPU OOMs on decode nodes (gk-12..gk-15). 55% client request drops detected since 17:06 UTC. Pager: miguel_oncall

miguel_oncall: I'm on it. initial hypothesis: runaway generation / max_tokens mismatch on a customer route. pulling recent deploys and logs.

alerts-bot: alert group: decode-ooms-streaming. avg gpu_free drops from 9GB->1GB in ~30s. errors: "CUDA out of memory" + "kv cache growth". affected routes: /v1/stream/generate (models: redwood-xxl-quant).

miguel_oncall: Tara, can you grep for unusual max_tokens in the router logs?

tara_sre: on it — running quick query: `jq -r '.request.max_tokens, .route' logs/*.json | grep -E "[0-9]{4,}" | sort -nr | head`

tara_sre: result: a batch of requests from api-key:cust-42 had max_tokens=20000 and streaming=true (timestamp 17:04-17:08). also found repeated retries (client backoff misconfigured).

ops_jake: rolling a quick mitigation: bump throttle for cust-42 and apply per-route max_tokens cap 1024 at the ingress layer. doing via: `rbctl routes update --id cust-42 --max_tokens 1024 --rate-limit 60r/m`

miguel_oncall: good. also switching affected traffic to smaller model variant (redwood-xxl-quant -> redwood-l-quant) as fallback. cmd: `rbctl route-override --route /v1/stream/generate --model redwood-l-quant --scope temp`

incident-bot: NOTE: automated fallback applied for 12m. Telemetry will report success/failure.

tara_sre: quick hotfix confirmed: CPU/GPU memory stabilized on gk-13 after throttle + model fallback. request drops reduced from 55% -> 6% in next 3m.

miguel_oncall: running soft restarts on gk-12,gk-14 to clear fragmented cuda heaps: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/decode-gk-12` (rolling across AZs). Doing one node at a time.

alerts-bot: saw two nodes (gk-12 gk-14) report container restarts during the rollout (OOM exit code). nodes recovered and rejoined.

customer-success-liz: pinging cust-42 with an interim summary: "We observed excessive max_tokens on your requests causing GPU OOMs and dropped responses. We've limited per-request tokens and applied a temporary model fallback; we're investigating root cause and will share next steps."

ops_jake: also added a short-term safety rule in the runtime: absolute token ceiling 16384 for streaming-enabled requests (enforced at routing). will revert after postmortem.

miguel_oncall: collecting traces and perf dumps — saving nvprof + dmesg logs. snippet from decode container:
```[17:05:12] ERROR decode: CUDA out of memory. attempted alloc 2.1GB
[17:05:12] WARN decode: kv_cache_capacity exceeded: 18M entries
[17:05:12] ERROR runtime: aborting request (drop)  conn=xyz123
```

tara_sre: filing a short RCA draft: likely chain: client misconfig or bug -> runaway generation (no per-request cap) -> kv-cache growth + fragmentation -> CUDA OOM -> container restarts -> request drops. Need to check if SDK retry loop amplified load.

miguel_oncall: immediate mitigations done. next: schedule deeper heap analysis, add prioritized QA for per-route max_tokens defaults, and add telemetry alert for token-growth anomalies.

incident-bot: ACTIONS: 1) mitigation applied (throttle + fallback + node restarts) 2) customer notified 3) follow-up postmortem -> assigned to tara_sre 4) incident resolved when request drops <2% for 15m.

alerts-bot: request drops at 17:40 UTC now 1.2% sustained.

miguel_oncall: closing active pager. will hand off to tara for postmortem. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

customer-success-liz: capturing the customer timeline and CSAT follow-up. will draft external note tomorrow.

tara_sre: postmortem created: PM-1768509999. Will include remediation: per-route token sane defaults, SDK guidance for retry/backoff, runtime kv-cache caps, and a test harness for streaming max_tokens. ETA for full RCA: 48hrs.
